Graeco-Latin square
may be thought of as "dimensions" along which a value may vary. Due to the mutually orthogonal property, there is exactly one instance somewhere in the table for any pair of elements, such as (white foreground, monospace), or ("fjords", navy background) etc., and also all possible such pairs of values of distinct "dimensions" are represented exactly once each. The above table therefore allows for testing five values in each of four different "dimensions" in only 25 observations instead of 625 (= 5) observations.
